question.problem:
Which of the following vector-valued functions are differentiable with respect to $t$ on $t\in (0,1)?$

$$
\begin{aligned}p(t) & =⟨2t-1,\,{t}^{2}+4,\,-{e}^{t}⟩ \\ q(t) & =⟨(t+1)^{4},\,\sqrt[3]{t},\,\operatorname{ln}⁡t⟩ \\ r(t) & =⟨3t+2,\,\operatorname{arctan}⁡t,\,{t}^{2}-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

choices.value: All the functions are differentiable on $t\in (0,1)$
None of the functions are differentiable on $t\in (0,1)$

current_example.problem: Is the vector function $\mathbf{f}(t) = \left\langle 2e^t, \: \dfrac{\pi}{t-3}, \: \sqrt{t} \right\rangle$ differentiable with respect to $t$ on $t \in [0, 2]?$
current_example.worked_solution:
The function is defined on $t \in [0, 2].$ Remember that a function is differentiable on the interval $[0, 2]$ if and only if all of its component functions are differentiable on that interval.

Let's now differentiate $\mathbf f(t)$ to find $\mathbf f'(t)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{\pi }{t-3}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{t})⟩ \\  & =⟨2{e}^{t},\,-\frac{\pi }{(t-3)^{2}},\,\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the third component of this vector, $\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}$ is undefined at $t = 0.$ Therefore, we conclude that the function $\mathbf f(t)$ is **not** differentiable on $[0,2].$
